title: Welcome to Programming
text: These questions check your understanding of what programming is, how computers and AI assistants differ, and how this book's examples work.

tasks.text: A recipe says "bake until golden brown." Why would an instruction like this cause trouble in a computer program?
choices: A computer can't use judgment to fill in what "until golden brown" means; every step has to be stated exactly.
Computer programs can't contain repeated steps.
The instruction is too short for a computer to read.

tasks.text: Which statement best describes the difference between a computer running code and an AI assistant answering a prompt?
choices: Both do exactly what they're told and nothing more.
Both guess what you meant when your instructions leave something out.
A computer does exactly what the code says; an AI assistant fills in whatever the prompt leaves out with its best guess.
An AI assistant does exactly what the prompt says; a computer guesses what the code means.

tasks.text: In this book's PARSE workflow, which step comes right after you ask an AI assistant for code?
When asked to "Write a JavaScript program that says hello," the assistant in this lesson made several decisions the prompt didn't specify. Name two of them.
tasks.answer: Any two of: the exact words ("Hello, World!"); adding a second version with a function; where the code runs (browser console, Node.js, or a web page with a popup); the punctuation style (semicolons at the ends of lines). Accept other reasonable decisions the student can point to in the reply.

tasks.text: If an AI assistant can write code for you, why is it still worth learning to read code? Give at least two reasons in your own words.
tasks.answer: Look for two of: someone has to judge whether the code is right; the assistant is guessing about your situation and can't see your data or goals; AI code can look correct but do something different from what you asked; code can do harmful things such as overwriting data, which you can only catch by reading it; you can't check code you can't read.

tasks.text: Open your AI assistant and send this prompt in a new chat: "Write a JavaScript program that says hello." (1) List every decision the assistant made that your prompt didn't specify. (2) Rewrite the prompt so it leaves less to guess: say what the message should be and where it should appear. (3) Send your new prompt in a new chat, and describe how the reply changed.
tasks.answer: Full credit: at least two unrequested decisions identified in the student's own reply; a rewritten prompt that specifies both the message and where it appears (for example, the console); an accurate description of how the second reply differs, such as fewer alternatives or exactly the requested output. Replies will vary, so grade the student's reasoning, not the specific code.
